discovery_sources.source_description: NIST AI 600-1, Generative AI Profile —

NIST SP 800-218A, AI-focused SSDF profile — NIST	Secure development across AI producers, integrators, and acquirers	P1/P2/P5; secure-AI development profile rather than duplicating generic SDLC controls

NIST adversarial machine learning taxonomy — NIST publications	Attack classes across learning methods, lifecycle stages, and attacker objectives	CP.1/CP.2 threat register; P1 and P5 tests. Check non-LLM coverage
OWASP Machine Learning Security Top 10 — OWASP	Model theft, extraction, poisoning, inference-time and training-related weaknesses	Broaden P1/P2/P5 beyond prompt injection and agents
OWASP AI Security Verification Standard — OWASP projects	Atomic verification requirements	Add requirement-level tests and implementation contracts; keep separate from AIVSS
CSA AI Controls Matrix — CSA	Control objectives, assurance, and responsibility allocation	All pillars; add individual control relationships and shared-responsibility fields
CoSAI security workstreams and Risk Map — CoSAI	Component, lifecycle, persona, and control relationships	P2 component inventory; cross-pillar responsibility modelling

ETSI Securing Artificial Intelligence publications — ETSI	Telecom-oriented AI threat, security, and assurance perspectives	P1/P2/P5; investigate infrastructure, distributed AI, and supply-chain boundaries

ISO/IEC 23894, AI risk management — ISO AI standards	Integration of AI risk into organizational risk processes	Cross-pillar risk acceptance and escalation; avoid treating technical controls as a complete risk process
ISO/IEC 42005, AI system impact assessment — ISO	Impacts on people and society, not merely security exposure	CP.3 enhancement or impact-assessment governance requirement
ISO/IEC 5338, AI system lifecycle processes — ISO	Lifecycle responsibilities and process completeness	P2 lifecycle records; P5 change gates; retirement requirements
ISO/IEC 8183, AI data lifecycle framework — ISO	Data lifecycle boundaries and responsibilities	P1 data governance; P2 lineage; P3 deletion/recovery relationships
ISO/IEC 24029 robustness-assessment family — ISO	Robustness assessment methods and assumptions	P5 evaluation methodology; distinguish adversarial robustness from general task reliability
ISO/IEC 5259 data-quality family — ISO	Quality of data used for analytics and ML	P1 validation; P2 data provenance; P5 quality acceptance criteria

IEEE 7000, ethical concerns in system design — IEEE Standards	Stakeholder values translated into engineering decisions	Cross-pillar impact governance; P2 design decisions; P4 stakeholder participation
UL 4600, autonomous-product safety — UL Standards	Safety-case reasoning and evidence for autonomy	CP.8 and P3/P5; embodied-system profile, not a generic software checklist
Guidelines for Secure AI System Development — UK NCSC	Secure design, development, deployment, operation, and maintenance	P1/P2/P5 lifecycle implementation guidance
UK AI assurance portfolio and guidance — UK government	Assurance techniques, appropriate use, and evidence limitations	P2 evidence quality; P5 independent assurance; assessor competence

Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI — IMDA	Accountability, ecosystem responsibilities, evaluation, and broader governance	Cross-pillar responsibilities; P4 transparency; P5 assurance
AI Verify testing framework/toolkit — AI Verify Foundation	Operationalizing testing and governance evidence	P2/P5 evidence adapters; do not equate a test result with certification
Australian Voluntary AI Safety Standard — Australian industry department	Organization-level guardrails and accountable deployment	Cross-pillar policy/impact governance; P4 contestability

Canadian Directive on Automated Decision-Making and impact assessment — Treasury Board	Impact-tiered public-sector decision governance	CP.3 classification; P4 explanations/recourse; government profile
OECD AI Principles and incident work — OECD AI	Accountability, human rights, robustness, and incident learning	CP.6 incident taxonomy; impact governance; P4 remedy
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI — UNESCO	Social, cultural, environmental, and rights impacts	Applicability-based governance topics; not automatic universal technical controls

Microsoft Responsible AI Standard — Microsoft Responsible AI	Organizational requirements, impact assessment, and accountable development	Cross-pillar AIMS governance; P2 decision records; P4 impact treatment
Microsoft AI security risk-assessment guidance — Microsoft Security	Practical AI security assessment and threat-analysis approaches	CP.2 and P5 assessment procedures; test reproducibility

AWS generative-AI security scoping matrix — AWS Security Blog	Security responsibilities change with consumption/integration/development scope	P2 deployment classification; inherited controls; provider/customer responsibility
Databricks AI Security Framework — Databricks	Data-platform and AI-stack security decomposition	P1/P2 infrastructure, data, model, and serving boundaries

Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy — Anthropic	Capability-triggered safeguards and escalation	CP.8; P5 dangerous-capability evaluation; avoid assuming frontier-lab thresholds fit ordinary deployments
OpenAI Preparedness Framework — OpenAI Safety	Capability assessment and deployment safeguards	CP.8/P5; record thresholds, uncertainty, and review authority
Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework — Google DeepMind	Frontier capability thresholds and response planning	CP.8; P3 containment; P5 capability-change gates
IBM AI Risk Atlas — IBM AI Risk Atlas	Risk descriptions spanning technical, organizational, and societal concerns	Expand risk vocabulary; link risks to assumptions and affected parties
MAS FEAT Principles — Monetary Authority of Singapore	Fairness, ethics, accountability, and transparency in financial decisions	P4 fairness/remedy; cross-pillar decision accountability
MAS Veritas assessment methodologies/toolkit — MAS	More operational assessment of financial-sector responsible-AI principles	P2/P5 metric selection, assessment records, and evidence

HKMA generative-AI and consumer-protection guidance — HKMA	Customer-facing financial use, protection, and institutional responsibility	Financial profile; P4 disclosure/recourse; CP.10 consequential actions

Federal Reserve/OCC model-risk guidance, SR 11-7 — Federal Reserve	Independent validation, effective challenge, limitations, and model inventory	P2 model inventory; P5 independent validation; explicit use restrictions
PRA SS1/23, model-risk management — Bank of England	Governance of model risk across organizational use	Cross-pillar accountability; P5 challenge; P2 inventory completeness
NAIC model bulletin on insurers’ AI use — NAIC	Insurer accountability, third parties, consumer outcomes, governance programs	Insurance profile; supplier evidence; P4 harmful-outcome monitoring
NYDFS insurance AI/external-data guidance — NYDFS	Underwriting/pricing, unfair discrimination, external data, and governance	P1 data admissibility; P4 fairness; P5 validation
FINOS AI Governance Framework — FINOS	Financial-services implementation and collaborative control practices	Financial profile; compare control language, evidence, and implementation patterns
Good Machine Learning Practice principles — FDA	Representative data, lifecycle quality, human-AI performance, and monitoring	P1 data quality; P4 human factors; P5 validation

FDA predetermined change-control-plan guidance for AI-enabled device software — FDA	Predefined, bounded changes with verification requirements	P5 material-change gates; P2 approved change envelope; medical-device profile
IMDRF SaMD clinical evaluation — IMDRF	Clinical association, analytical validation, and clinical validation	Separate technical accuracy from real-world clinical benefit
WHO guidance on large multimodal models in health — WHO	Health-specific LMM risks, governance, and stakeholder responsibilities	P4 harms and oversight; P5 multimodal evaluation; health profile
